name: dt_popc
prose: Function dt_popc(x) in libdtrace/dt_subr.c (lines 831-851), takes a ulong_t and returns a ulong_t, with no side effects. It has three compile-time variants. Under _ILP32 it applies the 32-bit parallel bit-count steps (constants 0x55555555, 0x33333333, 0x0F0F0F0F, then adding the shifted halves) and returns (x & 0x3F), the number of set bits of the 32-bit value. Under _LP64 it does the same with the 64-bit constants and one more shift by 32 and returns (x & 0x7F), the number of set bits of the 64-bit value (at most 64). If neither _ILP32 nor _LP64 is defined the body is empty (only a comment) and the function has no return statement, so it returns an indeterminate value in that configuration. The result is at most 32 in an ILP32 build and at most 64 in an LP64 build.
note: Reviewers: round 1 (the formal contract assumes 64-bit shifts, but there is an _ILP32 path where ulong_t is 32 bits) right; round 15 (the contract omits the no-side-effect guarantee and ignores the #else path with no return) right (dt_subr.c:833-850). Contract dropped because its form is only valid for one of the build variants. Tally 2 right 0 wrong.

name: static int dt_instr_size(uchar_t *instr, dtrace_hdl_t *dtp, pid_t pid, uintptr_t addr, char dmodel)
prose: Static function dt_instr_size(instr, dtp, pid, addr, dmodel) in libdtrace/i386/dt_isadep.c (lines 489-520; the slice 505-520 showed only its tail, so it is not an unnamed wrapper). It sets up a dtrace_dis_t describing the instruction bytes (instr, dtp, pid, addr) and a dis86_t whose byte-fetch callback is dt_getbyte (which reads the bytes and, for a byte that looks like the fasttrap trap instruction, asks the kernel with ioctl FASTTRAPIOC_GETINSTR on dtp->dt_ftfd for the original byte, ignoring a failed query). The cpu mode is SIZE32 when dmodel == PR_MODEL_ILP32 and SIZE64 for any other value. It calls dtrace_disx86(&x86dis, cpu_mode); a nonzero result returns -1. If the decoded instruction is one byte long and that byte equals FASTTRAP_INSTR (a breakpoint, possibly from another debugger) it returns -1. Otherwise it returns the decoded length d86_len. It takes no length parameter and does no length check of its own; the disassembler fetches bytes one at a time through the callback.
note: Old record was still-rejected as 'unnamed-x86-disassembler-wrapper' (mechanical). The function is dt_instr_size (dt_isadep.c:489). The old prose said the function returns -1 'if the length is too large' and requires the length to fit a buffer; no such parameter or check exists. No reviewer claim.

name: main
prose: main(argc, argv) of ctf/cvt/ctfmerge.c (lines 752-1019; the slice showed only the later part). It sets progname, reads debug_level from CTFMERGE_DEBUG_LEVEL, and parses getopt(":cd:D:fgl:L:o:tvw:s"): -c copy mode, -d and -D uniquify against a file and label, -f fuzzy matching, -g keep stabs, -l or -L label, -o output file, -t require CTF, -v verbose, -w additive merge file, -s dynsym; any other result calls usage() and exit(2). Validation: in copy mode no -d, -D, -l/-L, -o, -w or -s is allowed and exactly two operands are needed; otherwise -d with -w is rejected, -D needs -d, -o and a label are required and at least one input is needed; a failure calls usage() and exit(2). STRIPSTABS_KEEP_STABS in the environment turns on keep_stabs. A uniquify or with file that is not readable only produces a warning and is ignored; an output file that is not readable and writable calls terminate("Cannot open output file ..."). In copy mode it runs copy_ctf_data(argv[optind], argv[optind + 1], keep_stabs) and calls exit(0). Otherwise it sorts and de-duplicates the input file names; if count_files fails it calls terminate("Some input files were inaccessible"). It starts the work queue and worker threads and runs read_ctf over the inputs with merge_ctf_cb; if no CTF sections were found it prints a warning and calls exit(0). It then marks the queue finished, waits for the workers, joins them, and takes the single merged type tree mstrtd. With -d or -w it reads the reference file (terminate if it has no CTF data), terminates with "No room for additional types in master" if the reference's next type id is already a child id, merges into a new tree, adds the label, and either merges with the with-file data or records the parent label and name for the uniquified output; otherwise it relabels mstrtd and uses it directly. It writes the CTF with write_ctf to a temporary file name, renames it over the output file (a failed rename calls terminate), frees the temporary name and returns 0.
note: Reviewer round 15 (omits the terminate() path when the reference master has no room for additional types) right (ctfmerge.c:969-970). Tally 1 right 0 wrong. The whole function was read.

name: main
prose: main(argc, argv) of ctf/dump/dump.c (lines 913-1139; the slice showed its tail). It parses options d, f, h, l, s, S, t (selecting what to print through the global flags) and u (an output file) in a loop that also collects the single file operand. An option that getopt rejects is handled in the default case: if optopt is '?' (the user typed -?) it returns print_usage(stdout, 1); for any other illegal option letter it prints a warning and returns print_usage(stderr, 0). A second file operand, or no file operand, also returns print_usage(stderr, 0). With no print flags and no -u it selects all sections. It opens the file (failure calls die); if it is an ELF file it finds the .SUNW_ctf section (missing calls die) and, when present, the symbol and string tables; otherwise it mmaps the raw file (failures call die). It checks the preamble, the CTF magic and that the version is at least CTF_VERSION_2 (else die), and when the data is compressed inflates it with zlib, calling die on any failure. It then ORs into error the results of print_header (-h), print_labeltable (-l), read_data (-d or -S), read_funcs (-f or -S), read_types (-t or -S), read_strtab (-s or -S) and print_stats (-S). With -u it writes the header with the compress flag cleared followed by the uncompressed data to the file, and on an open or write failure it warns and ORs in E_ERROR. It ends the ELF handle and closes the input descriptor and returns error.
note: Reviewer round 15 (an unknown option is getopt's '?' and returns print_usage(stdout, 1), not print_usage(stderr, 0)) wrong: the code distinguishes optopt == '?' (stdout, verbose) from other illegal option letters (warn, stderr, non-verbose) (dump.c:955-959). The old prose lumped both cases. Tally 0 right 1 wrong. The whole function was read.

name: V_NAME_F1 (log1p)
prose: Generated vector function V_NAME_F1 (log1p) in aarch64/advsimd/log1pf.c (lines 41-55 with WANT_SIMD_EXCEPT, lines 71-80 otherwise; the vector-ABI name of the single-precision log1p, for example _ZGVnN4v_log1pf), taking a float32x4_t x and returning a float32x4_t whose lanes approximate log1p of the lanes of x. The documented worst-case error is about 1.69 ULP in the WANT_SIMD_EXCEPT build and 1.63 ULP otherwise (from the source comments). It first flags special lanes. Default build: lanes with x <= -1, and lanes where the comparison |x| <= 0x1p127 is false, which means |x| greater than 0x1p127 (including +/-infinity) or NaN. WANT_SIMD_EXCEPT build: lanes where (bits of |x|) - asuint(0x1p-23) is >= 0x4b800000 as unsigned, which means |x| < 0x1p-23 (including zeros and subnormals) or infinity or NaN, and lanes whose bit pattern as unsigned is >= asuint(-1.0f), which means x <= -1 (including -infinity and negative NaNs). If no lane is special it returns the inline polynomial log1pf_inline(x, ...). Otherwise special_case computes log1pf_inline for all lanes (in the WANT_SIMD_EXCEPT build the special lanes are first zeroed with v_zerofy_f32 so they raise no spurious floating-point exceptions) and replaces the special lanes with the result of the scalar log1pf on the corresponding input lane through v_call_f32; the scalar call may set exception flags or errno according to its own behaviour. It takes no locks and allocates no memory.
note: Reviewer round 15 (the default build also treats finite |x| > 0x1p127 as special, not only infinity and NaN) right (log1pf.c:73-74). The old prose said special lanes are x <= -1 or |x| >= infinity in both builds. The packet name was the expanded _ZGVnN4v_log1p; the definition head in the file is the macro. Tally 1 right 0 wrong.

name: V_NAME_D1_L1 (modf)
prose: Generated function V_NAME_D1_L1 (modf) in aarch64/advsimd/modf.c (lines 13-25), the two-lane double vector modf, taking float64x2_t x and double *out_int and returning the fractional parts. out_int must point to at least two writable doubles (16 bytes). It computes rounded = vrndq_f64(x), which rounds each lane toward zero, stores both lanes of rounded to out_int, forms x - rounded and clears (with vbicq) the lanes where x == rounded, so integral inputs including +/-infinity (for which inf - inf would be NaN) and -0.0 return +0; a NaN lane compares unequal and yields NaN, and its integer part stored is NaN; a negative non-integer lane returns a negative fraction. The source comment says it is exact in all rounding modes.
note: Name is the macro head as it appears in the file. No reviewer claim; prior prose checked (it already said truncated toward zero). Source: modf.c:13-25.

name: V_NAME_F1_L1 (modf)
prose: Generated function V_NAME_F1_L1 (modf) in aarch64/advsimd/modff.c (lines 13-26), the four-lane float vector modf, taking float32x4_t x and float *out_int and returning the fractional parts. out_int must point to at least four writable floats. It computes rounded = vrndq_f32(x), which rounds each lane toward zero (truncation, not round-to-nearest), stores the four lanes of rounded to out_int, forms x - rounded and clears the lanes where x == rounded, so integral inputs (including +/-infinity and -0.0) return +0, a NaN lane yields NaN, and for example 1.5 gives integer part 1 and fraction 0.5.
note: Reviewer round 15 (vrndq_f32 truncates toward zero, not round-to-nearest ties-to-even; the integer part of 1.5 is 1) right (modff.c:17-18); the old prose said round-to-nearest ties-to-even. Tally 1 right 0 wrong.

name: SV_NAME_F1 (acosh)
prose: Generated function SV_NAME_F1 (acosh) in aarch64/sve/acoshf.c (lines 30-42), the single-precision SVE acosh, taking an svfloat32_t x and a predicate pg and returning an svfloat32_t. It computes xm1 = x - 1, u = xm1 * (x + 1) and tmp = xm1 + sqrt(u), and flags as special the lanes of pg for which (asuint(x) - 0x3f800000) >= 0x20000000 as unsigned, i.e. all lanes except 1.0 <= x < 0x1p64 (so x < 1 including negatives, x >= 0x1p64, infinities and NaN are special). With no special lane it returns sv_log1pf_inline(tmp, pg), which is acosh(x) with a documented maximum error of about 2.47 ULP (source comment). Otherwise special_case recomputes x as xm1 + 1.0f, evaluates sv_log1pf_inline(tmp, svptrue_b32()) for all lanes and calls sv_call_f32(acoshf, x, y, special), which substitutes the scalar acoshf result for the special lanes; the scalar routine can set errno or floating-point exceptions, so the function is not free of side effects. The values in lanes inactive in pg are not specified by this code.
note: Reviewer round 15 (claims no side effects, but the special case calls scalar acoshf, which may set errno/fenv) right (acoshf.c:16-22; the errno claim is about the scalar library routine, not shown here). Also in the special path x is re-derived as (x - 1) + 1. Tally 1 right 0 wrong.

name: checkint
prose: Static inline function checkint(iy) in aarch64/sve/pow.c (lines 105-117); iy is the 64-bit pattern of a double. It extracts the biased exponent e = (iy >> 52) & 0x7ff. It returns 0 when e < 0x3ff (magnitude below 1, which includes all zeros and subnormals); 2 when e > 0x3ff + 52 (large magnitudes and also infinities and NaNs, whose exponent field is 0x7ff); otherwise it tests the bits of iy below the units position (a mask of (0x3ff + 52 - e) bits): any set returns 0 (not an integer), else if the bit at the units position is set it returns 1 (odd), else 2 (even). The sign bit is not looked at. The comment documents the argument as the bit representation of a non-zero finite value; for +0 or -0 the function returns 0, and for infinity or NaN it returns 2. It has no side effects.
note: Reviewer round 15 (the formal precondition allows -0, because iy != 0, though the prose requires a nonzero finite value) right; the contract is dropped. The old prose said the function returns 0/1/2 for 'nonzero finite' values only; the behaviour for the excluded inputs is now stated from lines 107-116. Tally 1 right 0 wrong.

name: doubletop
prose: Static function doubletop(x, scale) in math/test/rtest/dotest.c (lines 2198-2203), returns uint32. It sets e = 0x412 + scale, then while bit 0x100000 of x is clear it does x <<= 1 and e-- (shift_count times), and returns (e << 20) + x. Because x then has the bit 0x100000 set, the result equals ((0x413 + scale - shift_count) << 20) + (x_shifted - 0x100000): the high word of a double with exponent field 0x413 + scale - shift_count and a 20-bit mantissa field x_shifted - 0x100000. It requires 0 < x <= 0x1FFFFF (x = 0 loops forever; a bigger x with bit 20 clear shifts until overflow; a negative x makes the shifts undefined for a signed int) and, for a valid high word, a scale that keeps the exponent field in range; there are no checks. It has no side effects.
note: Reviewers: round 1 (prose misstates the fields: the exponent is result >> 20 and the mantissa is the normalised x minus 0x100000) right as a criticism of that older wording, the current text states it correctly; round 15 (the prose allows negative x, but the code left-shifts a signed int, which is undefined, and the contract requires x > 0) right. Tally 2 right 0 wrong.

name: floatval
prose: Static function floatval(x, scale) in math/test/rtest/dotest.c (lines 2205-2210), returns uint32. It sets e = 0x95 + scale, then while bit 0x800000 of x is clear it does x <<= 1 and e-- (shift_count times), and returns (e << 23) + x. Because x then has the bit 0x800000 set, the result equals ((0x96 + scale - shift_count) << 23) + (x_shifted - 0x800000): a single-precision bit pattern with exponent field 0x96 + scale - shift_count and mantissa field x_shifted - 0x800000. It requires 0 < x <= 0x7FFFFF (so between 1 and 23 shifts happen; x = 0 loops forever, a negative x makes the shifts undefined for a signed int) and a scale that keeps the exponent in range; there are no checks. It has no side effects.
note: Reviewers: round 1 (misstated fields) right for the older wording; round 15 (negative x allowed by the prose but the signed left shift is undefined, the contract requires x > 0) right. Tally 2 right 0 wrong.

name: static double RT (ulperr) (RT (float) got, const struct RT (ret) * p, int r, int ignore_zero_sign)
prose: Function-template RT (ulperr) in math/test/ulp.h (lines 40-100; instantiated per floating-point type by the NEW_RT mechanism), returns a double estimate of the error of got against the reference p->y, in ULPs. It reads p->y, p->tail and p->ulpexp and writes no memory; it works on a local copy want of p->y and may modify its own got. It returns 0.0 when got and want have identical bit patterns; when both are NaN it returns 0 if USE_MPFR is set and otherwise 0 when their signalling-ness matches and INFINITY when it does not; when the sign bits differ it returns 0.0 if ignore_zero_sign is set and got == want (the two zeros), INFINITY if ignore_zero_sign is not set or both values are nonzero, and otherwise continues; when exactly one of got and want is NaN it returns INFINITY; when got is infinite it replaces got by copysign(halfinf, got) and multiplies want by 0.5, and when want is infinite it replaces want by copysign(halfinf, want) and multiplies got by 0.5 (both, in that order, when both are infinite). Finally, for r == FE_TONEAREST it computes d = got - want and returns scalbn(d, -p->ulpexp) plus (-p->tail - 0.5) when d > 0 and plus (-p->tail + 0.5) otherwise; for another rounding mode it first moves got one step toward want with nextafter when (r is FE_DOWNWARD and got < want), (FE_UPWARD and got > want) or (FE_TOWARDZERO and |got| < |want|), and then returns scalbn(got - want, -p->ulpexp) - p->tail.
note: Reviewer round 15 (the claim that p->y is halved or replaced is false: the code modifies the local copy want and never p->y) right (ulp.h:43, 73-80). Tally 1 right 0 wrong.

name: long double tgamma128(long double x)
prose: Function tgamma128(x) in math/tgamma128.c (lines 173-356; the packet slice 253-358 showed the later part and the name tgamma does not exist in this file). It takes sign = signbit(x) and classifies x: a NaN returns x + x; zero returns 1/x (a division by zero giving +/-infinity); an infinity returns x - x (NaN, invalid) when negative and x when positive; a subnormal sets exponent = -16384; otherwise exponent = (frexpl exponent) - 1, i.e. floor(log2(|x|)). For a negative x it computes negadjust = sin_pi_x_over_pi(x), sets negative = true and x = -x; if negadjust is 0 (a negative integer) it returns negadjust / negadjust (NaN, invalid). It then selects by exponent: >= 11: a positive x returns huge * huge (overflow, +infinity) and a negative x returns tiny * tiny * negadjust (underflow with the sign of negadjust); 3 to 10: tgamma_large(x, negative, negadjust) is returned (it applies the negative adjustment inside); below -113: tgamma_ultratiny(...) and from -113 to -6: tgamma_tiny(...) are returned the same way; exponent 0: g = tgamma_central(x); from -5 to -1: g = tgamma_central(1 + x) / x; exponents 1 and 2 (x in [2, 8)): with i = (int)x, mult = x - 1 for i == 2 and a polynomial in t = x - (i + 0.5) for i = 3 to 7, and g = tgamma_central(x - (i - 1)) * mult. After those cases it returns g for a positive x and 1.0L / (g * x * negadjust) for a negative x. The function is inside a conditional section closed by #endif at line 358.
note: Old record was dropped as 'tgamma'. The real function is tgamma128 (tgamma128.c:173); the old prose also said the middle exponent range was [0,3) while exponent 0 is handled separately (lines 295-296) and the polynomial branch covers exponents 1 and 2. No reviewer claim (mechanical rejections only). Helpers tgamma_large, tgamma_tiny, tgamma_ultratiny and tgamma_central were not read; only their call conditions.

name: ATF_TC_BODY(rmdir_eperm, tc)
prose: Test body of ATF_TC_WITH_CLEANUP(rmdir_eperm) (fs_test.c:787-810). Nothing exists on entry: it initialises a path "test-dir/foo" (RE), requires that mkdir("test-dir", 0755) and mkdir("test-dir/foo", 0755) succeed, requires chmod("test-dir", 0555) to succeed and the path to exist, then calls atf_fs_rmdir(&p). If atf_user_is_root() it requires that no error was returned; otherwise it requires an error of type "libc" whose code is EACCES and frees it. It finalises the path. A cleanup function (lines 811-817) restores mode 0755 on test-dir.
note: Reviewer round 15 (the prose says test-dir exists on entry, but the body creates it) right (fs_test.c:794-797). Tally 1 right 0 wrong.

name: ATF_TC_BODY(mkdtemp_err, tc)
prose: Test body of ATF_TC(mkdtemp_err) (fs_test.c:875-894; its head requires an unprivileged user). It creates the directory "dir" with mode 0555 (ATF_REQUIRE on mkdir), initialises a path "dir/testdir.XXXXXX" (RE), calls atf_fs_mkdtemp(&p), requires that the result is an error of type "libc", checks non-fatally (ATF_CHECK_EQ) that its code is EACCES, frees the error, checks non-fatally (ATF_CHECK) that the path does not exist and that its string is still "dir/testdir.XXXXXX", and finalises the path.
note: Reviewer round 15 (the prose says dir exists on entry, but the body creates it) right (fs_test.c:880). Tally 1 right 0 wrong.

name: ATF_TC_BODY(mkstemp_err, tc)
prose: Test body of ATF_TC(mkstemp_err) (fs_test.c:1006-1028; its head requires an unprivileged user). It creates the directory "dir" with mode 0555 (ATF_REQUIRE), initialises a path "dir/testfile.XXXXXX" (RE), sets fd = 1234, calls atf_fs_mkstemp(&p, &fd), requires an error of type "libc", checks non-fatally that its code is EACCES, frees the error, and checks non-fatally that the path does not exist, that its string is unchanged and that fd is still 1234, then finalises the path.
note: Reviewer round 15 (the prose says dir exists and fd is 1234 on entry, but the body sets both) right (fs_test.c:1012-1015). Tally 1 right 0 wrong.

name: ATF_TC_BODY(mkdtemp_ok, tc)
prose: Test body of ATF_TC(mkdtemp_ok) (fs_test.c:825-866). It initialises two paths p1 and p2 with the template "testdir.XXXXXX" (RE), calls atf_fs_mkdtemp on each (RE), requires that the two resulting paths differ and both exist, and for each initialises an atf_fs_stat_t (RE) and requires that it is a directory with owner read, write and execute permission and no group or other permission; finally it finalises both stats and both paths. Failed ATF_REQUIRE checks stop the test case before the finalisation.
note: Reviewer round 15 (the prose says p1/p2 are initialised on entry, but the body initialises them) right (fs_test.c:830-831). Tally 1 right 0 wrong.

name: ATF_TC_BODY(list_append_list, tc)
prose: Test body of ATF_TC(list_append_list) (atf-c/detail/list_test.c:177-256), five independent blocks, each initialising its lists with RE and calling atf_list_append_list(&l1, &l2): (1) both lists empty: size of l1 is 0; (2) l1 has one element, l2 empty: size 1 and element 0 equals the item; (3) l1 empty, l2 has one element: size 1 and element 0 equals the item; (4) each has one element: size 2 with l1's item at index 0 and l2's at index 1; (5) both empty: the end iterators of l1 and l2 have different m_entry before the call, and after the call the end iterator of l1 has the m_entry that l2's end iterator had. The checks are ATF_CHECK (non-fatal), the RE calls are fatal. Each block finalises only l1; l2 is not finalised.
note: Reviewer round 15 (each block finalises its lists, but l2 is not finalised in the first four blocks) right, and also not in the fifth (list_test.c:188, 203, 218, 236, 254). Tally 1 right 0 wrong.

name: ATF_TC_BODY(find, tc)
prose: Test body of ATF_TC(find) (map_test.c:122-153). It initialises a map, inserts "K1" with the buffer val1 ("V1") and "K2" with val2 ("V2") (replace flag false, RE), requires that atf_map_find(&map, "K0") equals atf_map_end(&map), that finding "K1" does not equal the end and has key "K1" and data "V1", then overwrites that data in place with strcpy to "Z1", requires that a second find of "K1" returns data "Z1", requires that finding "K2" gives key "K2" and data "V2", and finalises the map. Failed requirements stop the test case before the finalisation.
note: No reviewer claim; prior prose checked.

name: ATF_TC_BODY(map_insert, tc)
prose: Test body of ATF_TC(map_insert) (map_test.c:237-269; the slice ended at line 255 in the middle of it). It initialises a map (RE), requires its size to be 0, inserts "K1", "K2" and "K3" each with the same string buffer buf (replace flag false, RE) and requires the sizes 1, 2 and 3 after the successive inserts. It then finds "K3" (must not be the end) and requires its data pointer to be buf, inserts "K3" again with buf2, requires the size to stay 3, finds "K3" again and requires the data pointer to be buf2, and finalises the map.
note: Old prose said the rest of the body was beyond the slice; I read the rest (map_test.c:256-269). No reviewer claim.
